A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same SphereAR research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including the relocated sample gallery.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet generation results, posterior and normalization ablations, and VAE-backbone experiments in Tables 1–4 and Figure 4.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds higher-resolution generation, timing measurements, high-CFG experiments and qualitative failure comparisons in Appendices E–I.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same hyperspherical VAE, Power Spherical posterior, hybrid backbone, causal Transformer, Rectified Flow head and final normalization after guided sampling. The added resolution and sampling-step configurations are evaluation settings, not new method components.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds ImageNet 512×512 class-conditional generation to the retained 256×256 evaluation. This extends resolution requirements within the same dataset and task; no new dataset or domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes the LlamaGen-XXL* and RandAR-XXL rows, retaining their smaller counterparts and the other comparators. The new timing and failure comparisons use existing baseline families, including MAR, VAR and LlamaGen.

E3.justification: V2 adds several evaluation designs: 512×512 training with KL coefficient 0.016 and 64 conditioning tokens; intermediate-checkpoint comparisons using training wall-clock time; single-A100 inference measurements across batch sizes 32–256 and 100/10/1 diffusion steps; and CFG testing up to 8. The existing 256×256 protocol is retained.

E4.justification: Appendices F–I substantially expand the analyses: checkpoint measurements examine convergence efficiency, sampling-step tests examine the inference bottleneck, higher-CFG tests examine robustness, and comparisons with MAR-L examine failure modes. The original posterior, normalization and backbone ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify evaluation on 50,000 samples drawn with a fixed random seed. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests; the added plots continue to present point estimates.

E6.justification: The retained 256×256 results, including SphereAR-B/L/H FIDs of 1.92/1.54/1.34 and Tables 2–4, are unchanged. V2 adds 512×512 SphereAR-L results of FID 1.67 and IS 292.5, plus checkpoint, throughput, high-CFG and failure-case findings. Table 1 drops the XXL baseline entries with FIDs 2.34 and 2.15.

T1.justification: The mathematical method exposition and Appendices A–B retain the same assumptions, projection lemmas, linearized refeeding bound and radial-KL derivation. No substantive definition, theorem or proof changes were found.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: fixed-radius hyperspherical latents stabilize continuous-token autoregression and support parameter-efficient image generation. The headline performance and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking convergence efficiency to dense autoregressive supervision and inference cost to the diffusion head. Appendix I newly discusses facial artifacts, illegible text and fine-detail failures, hypothesizes a dataset-related cause, and explicitly identifies ImageNet-only evaluation as a generalization limitation.

D1.justification: V2 documents settings for the added experiments, including the higher-resolution KL coefficient and conditioning-token count, eight-A100 training timing, and single-A100 inference measurements with specified batch sizes and sampling steps. Existing architecture details, training recipes and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix G adds Shortcut Models by Frans et al. and MeanFlow by Geng et al. as possible future inference accelerations. Section 2 otherwise retains the same cited research and positioning; the general citation-style conversion is presentational.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are preserved. Limited edits clarify the component ablation with numbered-row references, expand the appendix organization, add an LLM-use disclosure, update author/publication information and remove the acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 5 and Figures 6–9 for higher-resolution results, convergence, inference speed, robustness and failures. Table 2 becomes a standalone display with numbered rows, and the conference template reflows existing material. The original sample images are retained and renumbered from Figures 6–17 to Figures 10–21.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical assessment of SphereAR by addressing v1's missing evidence about autoregressive training and inference costs, higher-resolution behavior and practical failure boundaries. The timing studies, 512×512 evaluation and extended CFG tests support a more informed assessment of usefulness, while explicit limitations improve transparency. Removing two XXL baseline rows modestly reduces comparison coverage, but the retained main results and added evidence support a clear net improvement.
